newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance starts new polyester unit.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance starts new polyester unit.

text.p: Indian petrochemicals firm Reliance Industries Ltd said it commissioned its third plant to make polyester filament yarn at Hazira on the western coast.
The plant will have an annual capacity of 30,000 tonnes a year, Reliance said in a statement.
"Reliance is expected to commission another 30,000 tonnes PFY (polyester filament yarn) plant shortly, thereby taking the total PFY capacity to 210,000 tonnes per year," it said.
The firm said Indian demand for PFY during 1997/98 (April-March) is expected to cross 575,000 tonnes a year.

"This will represent a compounded growth rate in consumption of about 19 percent over the past 10 years. Reliance expects to enhance its market share from the existing 29 percent to nearly 37 percent in the next financial year," the statement said.
It said international PFY prices rose from a low of $1.10 per kg to $1.30 per kg recently.
At the Hazira works, Reliance also recently commissioned its second line of 175,000 tonnes of polypropylene capacity, thereby raising total polypropylene capacity to 350,000 tonnes a year.
It also expanded capacity of its PVC plant to 270,000 tonnes a year from 180,000 tonnes earlier this month, Reliance said.
Reliance Industries is India's largest private firm.
